Public affairs and ESG · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Legislative agenda alert

Patricia · Government Affairs Analyst

Forty priority bills on taxes, packaging and labeling are moving through 9 committees of the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate, tracked by a 2-person team at a consumer goods manufacturer.

When it runs
Every 2 hours on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, when the agenda pages of the 9 monitored committees and the Floor Order of Business are updated, with an extra check at 8 p.m. for agendas published after hours
What it delivers in production
Within 2 hours of the agenda being published, the team receives on Slack the priority bill that was included, with committee, date, rapporteur, company position and mapped counterpart. Priority 1 triggers a WhatsApp message to the director.
Who decides
Detects and alerts; the director decides on contact
Effort
Calibrate on 20 weeks; 3 weeks of observation
Set up5 steps · 11 ready files

# Agenda alert rules

## Matching
- An agenda item matches the list only when number, year and house are all equal. "PL 2.338/2024" on the agenda is the same as "PL 2338", year 2024, in the list.
- Same number with another year or another house: DISCARDED, with the reason.
- A request (requerimento) that cites a bill on the list is an inclusion of that bill, with type request.

## Item type
- Merits deliberation: vote on the report (parecer) or on the bill.
- Urgency request: request to vote under the urgency regime.
- Hearing request: request for a public hearing. It is not a deliberation.

## Action by tier (the highest one applies)
| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| Priority 3, or hearing request | Log in Slack, no alert |
| Priority 2 with merits | Slack alert to the internal owner, with draft |
| Priority 1 with merits; urgency request; merits with a session in less than 24 hours | WhatsApp to the director, calendar block within 1 hour, draft to legal if there are merits |

## Rules with no leeway
- Hours to the session count from the scan. E.g.: from Nov 17 at 2 p.m. to Nov 18 at 10 a.m. is 20 hours.
- Merits with less than 24 hours moves up a tier. E.g.: PLP 108/2024, priority 2, session in 20 hours: WhatsApp, calendar and draft.
- A hearing request stays as a log at any priority and deadline. E.g.: PL 4.501/2023, priority 1, in 21 hours: log only.
- WhatsApp carries only bill, committee and date and time. E.g.: "PL 2.338/2024, Chamber CMADS, Nov 19 at 10 a.m.". The company's position and the contact person stay in the Slack line.
- An unavailable source does not prove absence. E.g.: CCJC down: PL 777/2025 stays without a conclusion.
- Only the same number becomes a discard. E.g.: PL 2.338/2020 (the list has PL 2.338/2024): DISCARDED, other year. PL 9.104/2025 and PL 3.317/2025 are not on the list: they stay out, and the header shows 5 inclusions and 1 discard.
- The final answer, the run report and the STATE are outputs too: what a rule says to omit does not appear in them, not even to explain the exclusion.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent does not send a message to a legislator, staffer or civil servant under any circumstances; the note to the rapporteur is a draft that legal reviews and a person delivers. A hearing request is not a deliberation on the merits and does not trigger priority 1. The history of contacts with legislators is restricted to the team and to compliance. The WhatsApp message to the director carries only bill, committee and date; company position and counterpart names stay in internal Slack. The Agenda Reader uses a service account of the government affairs team with a read-only profile over public sources, and only the Notifier gets write scope in Notion. Who can see each employee is defined in Members and Permissions.

Common mistakes

  • Treating placement on the agenda as certainty of a vote; committee agendas have 20 to 40 items and most are not taken up in the session.
  • Mixing up bills from different years or alerting on the attached bill instead of the main one with the substitute text.
  • Reading only the committee agenda and ignoring an urgency request on the Floor, which pulls the bill out of the committees.
  • Alerting without stating the rapporteur's position, so the team spends the lead time finding out about the report instead of acting on it.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Lead time between agenda publication and alert to the teamfrom about 6 hours after manual discovery to up to 2 hours after publicationestimate based on the described routine
Priority bills voted without a prior alertfrom 5 a year to 0 to 1estimate based on the described routine
False alerts per session week1 or fewer, measured in calibrationestimate based on the described routine

Fictional sample. Sweep of 2026-09-01 at 4 p.m. Sources: agendas of 9 committees and the Order of Business. 3 inclusions detected, 1 false positive discarded.

Y, favorable report with substitute text published today | company position: opposed to art. 7 of the substitute | mapped counterpart: aide to the committee chair, last contact 2026-07-14 | ACTION: WhatsApp to the director sent; prep block created on the manager's calendar for 2026-09-02 at 9 a.m.; draft note to the rapporteur attached for legal review

PRIORITY 2 | Bill PLP 108/2024 (IBS regulation, credit provisions) | Senate, CAE | agenda of 2026-09-02 | rapporteur: Sen. Z | position: support with amendment | ACTION: alert on the team's Slack; suggested contact with the industry association

PRIORITY 3 | Bill PL 4.501/2023 (front-of-pack labeling) | Chamber, Consumer Protection Committee | agenda of 2026-09-03 | hearing request only, no deliberation on the merits | ACTION: logged on Slack, no alert

DISCARDED: Bill PL 2.338/2020 (similar number, different topic).
NOTION UPDATES AWAITING APPROVAL: 2.
